# `liber:tpm@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:tpm` package (`tpm.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem TPM 2.0 - random bytes, PCRs read and extended, secrets sealed to a PCR's value, and quotes, as typed operations over the machine's one TPM.  THREE PARTIES, THREE INTERFACES. An APPLICATION holds a `tpm` connection minted for ONE of three grants and carrying that grant's operations only. PERMISSIONMANAGER holds the private `tpm-admin` endpoint that mints those connections. The TPM DRIVER serves `tpm-device`, and TpmService is its one consumer.  NOTHING RAW CROSSES ANY OF THEM. There is no command passthrough: a raw TPM command interface is an authority over every session and every hierarchy of the machine, which is exactly what a third-party API must not be. Every operation below is built by the driver's library from typed arguments.  WHAT A CALL COSTS. `seal`, `unseal` and `quote` each generate a primary key in the TPM, which takes a TPM tens to hundreds of milliseconds; `random`, `pcr-read` and `pcr-extend` are one short command each. One call is outstanding per connection and sixteen in all, and the TPM runs one at a time.

## Types

### enum `outcome`

HOW A CALL ENDED. Every answer carries one: `done` with its value, or the refusal by name.

| case | ordinal | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `done` | 1 |  |
| `not-granted` | 2 | The connection's grant does not carry this operation. |
| `pcr-not-allowed` | 3 | `pcr-extend` of a PCR other than 16 or 23, or any operation naming a PCR past 23. |
| `bounds` | 4 | A count, secret or nonce past its bound. |
| `busy` | 5 | A call is already outstanding on this connection, or sixteen are waiting in all. |
| `policy-refused` | 6 | `unseal` of a secret whose PCR no longer holds the value it was sealed to. |
| `owner-hierarchy-unavailable` | 7 | The owner hierarchy has an authorization value or is disabled, so `seal`, `unseal` and `quote` cannot run. |
| `other-component` | 8 | `unseal` of a secret another component sealed. |
| `interrupted` | 9 | The call reached the driver and the driver went away before answering. It is NEVER replayed: an extend may have reached the TPM, and a replay would extend twice. A caller that must know reads the PCR. |
| `unavailable` | 10 | No TPM is being served: none was found, or its driver is restarting. |
| `tpm` | 11 | The TPM answered with its own response code, in `code`. |
| `fault` | 12 | The TPM's interface failed or its answer could not be read. |

### record `quote`

A QUOTE: the attestation the TPM made, its ECDSA P-256 signature (r, s), the public point (x, y) of the key that signed it for verification elsewhere, and the PCR digest the attestation carries. The key is not certified by the TPM's endorsement key, so a verifier learns it on first use.

## Interfaces

### interface `tpm`

THE APPLICATION'S CONNECTION, carrying the operations of the one grant it was minted for.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `info` | `info() -> result<info-answer, error>` | The interface, the TPM's identity, and whether sealing works. Every grant. |
| 2 | `random` | `random(count: u32) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` | At most 1024 bytes from the TPM's generator. The `tpm` grant. |
| 3 | `pcr-read` | `pcr-read(pcr: u32) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` | PCR 0-23 of the SHA-256 bank. The `tpm` grant. |
| 4 | `pcr-extend` | `pcr-extend(pcr: u32, digest: list<u8>) -> result<status, error>` | Extend PCR 16 or 23 with a SHA-256 digest: the PC Client profile's debug and application PCRs. 0-7 are the firmware's, 8-15 are this system's own measured boot's, 17-22 the dynamic root of trust's. PCRs are SHARED by the whole machine. The `tpm-measure` grant. |
| 5 | `seal` | `seal(pcr: u32, secret: list<u8>) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` | Seal at most 96 bytes to PCR 0-23's present value; the sealed object opens only on this TPM, only while that PCR holds that value, and only for the component that sealed it. The `tpm-seal` grant. |
| 6 | `unseal` | `unseal(sealed: list<u8>) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` | The secret a sealed object holds. The `tpm-seal` grant. |
| 7 | `quote` | `quote(pcr: u32, nonce: list<u8>) -> result<quote-answer, error>` | A quote of PCR 0-23 over a nonce of at most 64 bytes. The `tpm` grant. |

### interface `tpm-admin`

THE MINTING ENDPOINT, PermissionManager's alone. The connection carries one grant's operations for the named component, and lives as long as `owner` does and no longer, however it is copied.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mint` | `mint(kind: grant, component: string, owner: handle<task>) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |

### interface `tpm-device`

THE PROVIDER CONTRACT a `tpm` publication serves - to TpmService alone. It executes ONE OPERATION AT A TIME, WHOLE, in the order received: a TPM runs one command at a time, and an operation interleaved between another's `CreatePrimary` and its `FlushContext` would exhaust the objects the first one needs. It decides nothing about who may do what; the bounds are the library's own.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `describe` | `describe() -> result<device-description, error>` |  |
| 2 | `random` | `random(count: u32) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` |  |
| 3 | `pcr-read` | `pcr-read(pcr: u32) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` |  |
| 4 | `pcr-extend` | `pcr-extend(pcr: u32, digest: list<u8>) -> result<status, error>` |  |
| 5 | `seal` | `seal(pcr: u32, secret: list<u8>) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` | A secret of at most 128 bytes sealed to a PCR's present value, as the sealed object's bytes. |
| 6 | `unseal` | `unseal(sealed: list<u8>) -> result<bytes-answer, error>` |  |
| 7 | `quote` | `quote(pcr: u32, nonce: list<u8>) -> result<quote-answer, error>` |  |
